title: The Haystack He Could Not Name: Moscow, Murnau, the Bauhaus, and the Object Removed from Painting
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Moscow, born to the tea merchant
stops.date_confidence: attested; the birth address is not identified in any source reached this pass, and the pin sits at the city centre as a placeholder
stops.campa: A son is born in Moscow to Vasily Silvestrovich Kandinsky, a tea merchant whose trade runs east to Kyakhta on the Chinese border, and to Lidia Ivanovna Ticheeva. They give him his father's name. The house is not recorded; the trade is. Tea comes overland in chests and the family money is made moving it west. The boy will spend the first thirty years of his life inside the professions his class expects of him, law and political economy and a university lectureship, before he takes up a brush in earnest.
suggested_refs: The Kyakhta tea route, source of the Kandinsky family's Moscow fortune
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Odessa, the piano and the cello
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia dates the start of the music lessons to 1871; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The pin is the Odessa city centre; neither the household nor the gymnasium address was confirmed
stops.campa: His parents separate and the boy is raised in Odessa, largely by his aunt Elizaveta Ticheeva, in a household that sends him to the classical gymnasium and puts him at the keyboard. The lessons begin in 1871, when he is four. He learns piano; he learns cello; he draws. Forty years later, when he tries to write down what a colour does to a person, every word he reaches for comes out of this room: keys, strings, the trumpet, the double bass, the organ.
stops.quote: Colour is the keyboard, the eyes are the hammers, the soul is the piano with many strings. The artist is the hand which plays, touching one key or another, to cause vibrations in the soul.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: The Richelieu classical gymnasium of Odessa, and the household of Elizaveta Ticheeva
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Vologda, inside the painted house
stops.date_confidence: the expedition is attested to 1889; the month is unknown and supplied to order the segment, the day defaulted. The villages he actually visited are not named in reachable sources and the pin sits on the city of Vologda
stops.campa: The law faculty sends the student north into the Vologda forests to record the customary law of the Komi, whom Russians then call Zyrians. He takes down peasant judgments and pagan survivals, and he walks into houses painted over every surface, walls and ceiling and furniture and stove, with ornament that leaves no plank bare. He writes afterwards that stepping inside them was like being able to move about within a painting. He is twenty-two. The article he publishes out of the journey is about Zyrian customary law.
stops.quote: The vermilion now rings like a great trumpet, or thunders like a drum.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's own 1889 ethnographic article on Zyrian customary law, and the painted peasant interiors of the Vologda region
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Moscow University, the law degree and the cousin
stops.date_confidence: the degree, the lectureship in jurisprudence and the marriage to Anna Chimiakina are all attested to 1892; months and days unknown and defaulted. The pin is the historic university building on Mokhovaya, not a verified lecture hall
stops.campa: He takes his degree in law and political economy, works under the economist Aleksandr Chuprov, writes on the legality of labourers' wages, and is kept on to lecture in jurisprudence. The same year he marries his cousin Anna Chimiakina, whom the family call Anja. Four years later the University of Dorpat offers him a chair. He is thirty years old, married, salaried, and one signature away from being a professor of law in the Russian Empire. Every one of those facts is abandoned inside a single year.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's student thesis on the legality of labourers' wages, Imperial Moscow University
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Bolshoi Theatre, hearing Lohengrin
stops.date_confidence: [R] the episode survives only in Kandinsky's own memoir Rueckblicke, written some twenty years afterwards; no performance date, no independent witness. Year and month supplied to order the segment
stops.campa: At the Bolshoi he hears Richard Wagner's Lohengrin, and in the memoir he writes twenty years later he does not say he heard it. He says he saw it: the whole of Moscow, all his own colours, the wild lines of the last hour before sunset, standing in front of him in the sound. Wagner had wanted the arts welded into one work and argued the case in print for decades. Kandinsky takes the welding privately, as a report on how his own senses behave. He is a law lecturer, with no professional use for any of it. He sets the evening down eighteen years afterwards, in a Berlin pamphlet for Der Sturm.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky, Rueckblicke (1913), on the Lohengrin performance and the colours of Moscow at sunset
sources: dossier synthesis, flagged as autobiographical and uncorroborated

stops.name: Moscow, the haystack he cannot name
stops.date_confidence: [R] the French exhibition in Moscow is independently documented; the failure of recognition is Kandinsky's own later account in Rueckblicke. Month and day supplied. An earlier research pass labelled this stop 'Munich exhibition hall' while giving Moscow coordinates: the Monet was seen in Moscow, before he left Russia, and the label was wrong
stops.campa: A French exhibition reaches Moscow with Claude Monet's haystacks in it. Kandinsky stands in front of one and cannot find the object in it. The catalogue tells him it is a haystack; he is annoyed with the painter for not making that plain, and then notices that the picture has hold of him regardless, that the colour by itself is doing the work the subject was supposed to do. He refuses the Dorpat chair. Before the year is out he has left for Munich to learn to draw, and he turns thirty that December in a foreign city.
stops.quote: Generally speaking, colour is a power which directly influences the soul.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: The 1896 French art exhibition in Moscow, and Monet's Haystacks series

stops.name: Munich, the drawing school of Anton Azbe
stops.date_confidence: the Munich study period is given by Wikipedia as 1896-1900 without a break; standard biographies put him with Azbe roughly 1897-1899, and one consulted source says 'through 1898'. The endpoint is unsettled and is left loose here. Month and day defaulted; the pin approximates Schwabing, the school's street address unconfirmed
stops.campa: In Anton Azbe's private school in Schwabing he draws from the model beside other Russians, among them Alexej von Jawlensky and Marianne von Werefkin, in a city where a foreigner with money can study painting without an academy's permission. He is thirty, a decade older than the students around him, and pays for his place out of the family tea money. Azbe teaches the head as ball and plane. His pupil is bored by the nude and keeps slipping out to paint small landscapes on cardboard, laying the colour on with a palette knife.
suggested_refs: Anton Azbe's private school, Schwabing, and its Russian colony of the later 1890s
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Munich Academy, the class of Franz von Stuck
stops.date_confidence: admission to Stuck's class in 1900 after an earlier rejection is attested; the October date is inherited from paul_klee.journey.json, which places both men entering the same class at nearly the same moment. The coordinate is inherited byte-identical from that file and sits roughly 380 m south of the Akademiestrasse building given by German Wikipedia at 48.1531, 11.5803; the discrepancy is left for the operator rather than split
stops.campa: Rejected once, he is taken at the second attempt into the painting class of Franz von Stuck, reckoned the first draughtsman in Germany. Stuck tells him his palette is too loud and sets him to work a year in grey. Into the same class, in the same weeks, comes a twenty-year-old Swiss violinist's son called Paul Klee. They will be colleagues for three decades at a school neither of them has heard of, and neighbours in a house that has not been built.
suggested_refs: Franz von Stuck's painting class, Akademie der Bildenden Kuenste Muenchen, 1900-1901
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Munich, Phalanx and the students the academy refuses
stops.date_confidence: the founding of Phalanx is attested to 1901 and Kandinsky's presidency with it; month and day unknown and defaulted. The pin is an approximate Schwabing location, the school's street address unverified
stops.campa: He founds Phalanx with a group of Munich painters, is made its president, designs its poster, and runs an exhibition society and a school together on the premise that the academies keep out whoever matters. Eleven exhibitions in four years bring Monet to Munich along with the Neo-Impressionists. The school takes women students, whom the state academy will not enrol on any terms. Into the summer class of 1902 comes one of them, Gabriele Muenter, twenty-five years old and lately refused by that academy.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's 1901 Phalanx poster, and the eleven Phalanx exhibitions of 1901-1904
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Kallmuenz, the ring given at the summer class
stops.date_confidence: CORRECTED from an earlier pass, which put this at Kallmuenz in 1902: German Wikipedia's 'Gabriele Muenter' gives Kochel am See for the summer of 1902 and Kallmuenz for the summer of 1903, and dates the beginning of the affair to Kallmuenz. Month approximate, day defaulted; the coordinate is corrected about 5 km west of an earlier pin
stops.campa: The summer painting class moves to Kallmuenz in the Oberpfalz, a stone town under a ruined castle above the Naab. Here the teacher and the student stop pretending. Kandinsky is thirty-six and married in Moscow; Muenter is twenty-six and has been kept out of the state academy for being a woman. He gives her a ring and calls it an engagement. The engagement runs thirteen years, through Tunisia and Sevres and Murnau, and never becomes a marriage. The divorce from Anja comes through in 1911.
suggested_refs: The Phalanx summer painting course at Kallmuenz, 1903

stops.name: Kairouan, four months of North African light
stops.date_confidence: [R] the Tunisian journey with Muenter is attested for the winter of 1904-05; Kairouan is the town standard biographies name and it was not confirmed as an itinerary stop in this pass. Month and day supplied to order the segment
stops.campa: They winter in Tunisia, out of Germany from the autumn of 1904 into the spring: four months of white walls, hard shadow and a light that makes European tonal painting look like an indoor habit. He is thirty-eight and has been painting for eight years. In that light a wall stops being a wall and becomes a plane of colour with its own behaviour, and the tonal habits of a Munich life class have nothing to say about it. He works small, in tempera and on cardboard: riders, markets, the flat fronts of buildings.
stops.quote: Keen lemon-yellow hurts the eye in time as a prolonged and shrill trumpet-note the ear, and the gazer turns away to seek relief in blue or green.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's Tunisian tempera panels of 1904-1905
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Sevres, the year outside Paris
stops.date_confidence: the Sevres residence is corroborated by two sources; the villa name Beau-Sejour circulates but was not confirmed by anything fetched this pass and is not asserted here. The coordinate is corrected about 650 m east to the town centre. Month approximate, day defaulted
stops.campa: They take a house at Sevres outside Paris for a year, and he sends work to the Salon d'Automne and the Salon des Independants in the seasons when Matisse and the Fauves are the scandal. He paints little. He is forty, has been a painter for ten years, and is turning out folk-tale scenes in tempera, Russian towns and horsemen, competent and behind the moment. In the same rooms Muenter is painting better than he is. Afterwards they move through Dresden, Brussels and the Netherlands.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's exhibits at the Salon d'Automne and the Salon des Independants, 1906-1907
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Munich, the Neue Kuenstlervereinigung founded
stops.date_confidence: the association is founded in January 1909 with Kandinsky as its first president; the day is unknown and defaulted. The pin is an approximate central Munich placeholder, the founding address not identified
stops.campa: Back in Munich he gathers Jawlensky, Werefkin, Muenter, Erbsloeh and Kanoldt into a new exhibiting body, the Neue Kuenstlervereinigung Muenchen, and is made its first president. It exists to hang what the Secession will not. Into the same association comes a Russian dancer, Alexander Sakharoff, who works with Kandinsky and the composer Thomas von Hartmann on the plain question of what a colour has to do with a sound. Within three years the association will refuse a painting of Kandinsky's own.
suggested_refs: The Neue Kuenstlervereinigung Muenchen and its international exhibitions of 1909-1911
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Murnau am Staffelsee, the Russenhaus
stops.date_confidence: Muenter buys the house in 1909; the month is approximate and the day defaulted. The Kottmuellerallee address comes from general knowledge and was not re-confirmed from a fetched page, though the Murnau residence itself is well corroborated
stops.campa: Muenter buys a house with a garden above the Staffelsee and the town starts calling it the Russenhaus. They paint the stair rail and the furniture themselves in the manner of the reverse-glass pictures made in these villages, saints and horsemen laid on black grounds, which they buy from farmhouses and copy. The mountains behind the town enter the canvases as bands of colour, and over about three years they stop being mountains. Jawlensky comes, and Werefkin, and Franz Marc, and Arnold Schoenberg.
suggested_refs: The Muenter Haus at Murnau and its collection of Bavarian reverse-glass paintings

stops.name: Ainmillerstrasse, the canvas standing on its side
stops.date_confidence: [R] the episode survives only in Kandinsky's Rueckblicke, with no date, no witness and no identification of the canvas; the year is supplied to order the segment. The Ainmillerstrasse address comes from general knowledge and was not confirmed this pass
stops.campa: The story he tells afterwards runs like this. He comes into the studio at dusk and sees a painting of extraordinary beauty, lit from inside, in which he can make out no subject at all. He goes closer. It is one of his own, standing on its side. In the morning the effect will not come back. What he takes from the accident is that the object had been in the way the whole time, and that a picture can be built from colour and line alone if the maker can find what compels each mark. He names that compulsion inner necessity.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky, Rueckblicke (1913), the sideways-canvas episode

stops.name: Munich, Concerning the Spiritual in Art finished
stops.date_confidence: the manuscript is completed in 1910; Piper issues the book at the end of 1911 with an 1912 imprint, which is why sources date it both ways. Month supplied to order the segment, day defaulted. The pin is central Munich for the publisher, not a verified address
stops.campa: He finishes the manuscript of Ueber das Geistige in der Kunst. It argues that form is nothing but the boundary between colours, that each colour and each shape carries a spiritual value which acts on the soul without passing through the subject, and that an artist with nothing to say has no business mastering form. It sorts his own work into three kinds: Impressions taken from nature, Improvisations welling up unplanned, Compositions built slowly. Piper prints it late in 1911. Michael Sadleir puts it into English in 1914.
stops.quote: THE ARTIST MUST HAVE SOMETHING TO SAY, FOR MASTERY OVER FORM IS NOT HIS GOAL BUT RATHER THE ADAPTING OF FORM TO ITS INNER MEANING.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914); rendered in small capitals in that edition
suggested_refs: Ueber das Geistige in der Kunst, R. Piper, Munich, 1911 with 1912 imprint; Sadleir's English edition of 1914
sources: Project Gutenberg ebook 5321, Concerning the Spiritual in Art

stops.name: Munich, the letter to Schoenberg
stops.date_confidence: the correspondence with Schoenberg is generally dated to January 1911, following the Munich performance of the Second String Quartet; that month could not be independently confirmed in this pass and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: He hears Arnold Schoenberg's Second String Quartet played in Munich and writes to the composer, a stranger to him, within the month. The letter says that what Schoenberg has done to the key, dissolving it while keeping the music under government, is what he himself is trying to do to the object. Schoenberg writes back. They correspond for years and exchange paintings, and Schoenberg's own canvases hang in the first Blue Rider exhibition that December.
stops.quote: In music a light blue is like a flute, a darker blue a cello; a still darker a thunderous double bass; and the darkest blue of all-an organ.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: The Kandinsky-Schoenberg correspondence, begun January 1911
sources: dossier synthesis, month precision flagged as uncorroborated

stops.name: Moderne Galerie Thannhauser, the rival exhibition
stops.date_confidence: the first Blaue Reiter exhibition opens 18 December 1911, attested; the jury's rejection of Composition V falls earlier the same month. The Theatinerstrasse gallery address comes from general knowledge and was not re-confirmed from a fetched page
stops.campa: The association's jury refuses Composition V, invoking a rule about size. Kandinsky, Muenter and Marc resign that day, and inside a fortnight the three of them hang a rival show in Heinrich Thannhauser's Moderne Galerie, in rooms alongside the association's own exhibition. Forty-three works. They call it Der Blaue Reiter, after a rider Kandinsky had painted and a colour Marc believed in. Delaunay sends from Paris. Schoenberg's paintings hang. Klee comes to look and joins the second exhibition in the spring.
stops.quote: Blue is the typical heavenly colour.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: The first Der Blaue Reiter exhibition, Moderne Galerie Heinrich Thannhauser, Munich, December 1911

stops.name: Munich, the almanac and The Yellow Sound
stops.date_confidence: Piper publishes Der Blaue Reiter Almanach in 1912; the May date is the usual one and the day is defaulted. Der gelbe Klang is written about 1909 and printed in the volume
stops.campa: The almanac comes out from Piper, edited by Kandinsky with Franz Marc: Bavarian glass saints set beside Picasso, Russian folk prints beside Egyptian shadow puppets, children's drawings, masks from Cameroon and the Pacific, and printed scores by Schoenberg, Berg and Webern. The argument is made by the sequence, not by the essays. Bound into it is his own stage piece, Der gelbe Klang, five scenes of colour, light, wordless voices and moving giants, with music by Thomas von Hartmann. Nobody performs it while he lives.
stops.quote: Yellow is the typically earthly colour. It can never have profound meaning.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: Der Blaue Reiter Almanach, R. Piper, Munich, 1912, containing Der gelbe Klang

stops.name: Goldach on Lake Constance, out of Germany in a week
stops.date_confidence: the flight into Switzerland in the first days of August 1914 is attested; the specific town of Goldach comes from general knowledge and was not re-confirmed, and the latitude is corrected about 1 km south from a pin that fell out over the lake. The day is approximate
stops.campa: Germany and Russia go to war and he is an enemy alien in the country he has painted in for eighteen years. He and Muenter cross to Switzerland within days and take rooms by Lake Constance. He is forty-seven. Everything stays behind in Munich and at Murnau: the canvases, the studio, the furniture, the boxes. The Munich flat is left as it stands. They keep house on the lake three months. In November he travels on alone through Zurich and the Balkans to Moscow, and she goes north to Sweden.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's and Muenter's Swiss months on Lake Constance, autumn 1914
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Moscow, back in the country he left at thirty
stops.date_confidence: the return to Moscow at the end of 1914 is attested; the month is approximate and the day defaulted
stops.campa: He reaches Moscow in the winter, forty-eight years old, a painter with a German career he cannot get to and a Russian standing he has not used in twenty years. For nearly two years he paints almost nothing. This is not Munich: there are Suprematists here, and Tatlin's counter-reliefs, and men fifteen years younger who file his spiritual triangle under mysticism. The war has taken the studio out from under him and he is beginning again from nothing. The domes and the horsemen come back into the work.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's Moscow canvases of 1916-1917 and the Russian avant-garde milieu of Malevich and Tatlin

stops.name: Stockholm, the last meeting with Muenter
stops.date_confidence: the final meeting in Stockholm is attested to 1916; the month is approximate and the day defaulted. The pin is the city, the Gummesons Konsthall address not confirmed
stops.campa: He comes to Stockholm in 1916 to exhibit and to see Muenter, and they meet for the last time. He is forty-nine and still writing to her about the marriage promised at Kallmuenz thirteen years earlier. He goes back to Moscow, and within the year has married someone else without telling her; she learns of it at second hand. The paintings stay where he left them in 1914. She keeps everything of his that is under her roof: oils, watercolours, sketchbooks, glass paintings, prints.
suggested_refs: The Gummesons Konsthall exhibitions of Kandinsky and Muenter, Stockholm, 1916

stops.name: Moscow, the marriage to Nina Andreevskaya
stops.date_confidence: attested to 11 February 1917, a fortnight before the February Revolution
stops.campa: He marries Nina Nikolaevna Andreevskaya, a general's daughter of about seventeen or eighteen. He is fifty. They honeymoon in Finland. By the time they are home the Tsar has abdicated, and over the next two years the flats, the accounts and what is left of the family tea money become nothing at all. Nina will outlive him by thirty-six years and spend all of them as the keeper of his estate, and the widow's version of his life is the one most of the century reads.
suggested_refs: Nina Kandinsky, Kandinsky und ich (1976), the widow's memoir

stops.name: Moscow, the two and a half years of Vsevolod
stops.date_confidence: the death in June 1920 is attested; the birth is given as September 1917 by the dossier and as 'the end of 1917' by Wikipedia, an unresolved discrepancy between sources. Day defaulted
stops.campa: A son is born and they call him Vsevolod, Lodya in the house. He lives about two and a half years and dies in June 1920, in the middle of the civil war and its hungry winters. Kandinsky does not write about it afterwards, and the paintings of those years are thin and few; he is at that point sitting on committees for the new state. There are no other children. Nina's memoir, written half a century later, gives the boy a few lines. What killed him is not in the record.
suggested_refs: The death of Vsevolod Kandinsky, Moscow, June 1920

stops.name: Moscow, the institute that throws out his programme
stops.date_confidence: Kandinsky serves in the visual arts section of Narkompros from 1918, teaches at the Free State Art Studios and later VKhUTEMAS, and is INKhUK's first director in 1920; the institutional detail rests on the dossier and general encyclopedia chronology and was not separately verified. Month supplied to order the segment; the pin is an approximate central Moscow placeholder
stops.campa: The revolution puts him to work: the visual arts section of Narkompros, a teaching post at the Free State Art Studios, a network of provincial museums founded across Russia, and then the first directorship of a new Institute of Artistic Culture. He proposes a research programme into how colour and form act on the nervous system, with questionnaires. Rodchenko, Stepanova and Popova throw it out as subjective mysticism and turn the institute toward construction and production. He withdraws from it.
stops.quote: The spiritual triangle moves slowly onwards and upwards.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: The INKhUK programme of 1920 and the Constructivist rejection of Kandinsky's psychophysical method

stops.name: Berlin, out of Soviet Russia with a mission's papers
stops.date_confidence: the departure in December 1921 is attested, legal and made on a nominal cultural mission; the day is defaulted
stops.campa: He and Nina leave for Berlin, legally, on the papers of a cultural mission, and do not go back. The Munich pictures and the crates are in Muenter's keeping and she is not answering letters about them. The Sturm gallery, which had sold him before the war, is not what it was. He is fifty-five and twice displaced, with the entire product of his best decade held by a woman he jilted. They wait out a Berlin winter in rented rooms. In the spring a letter comes from Weimar.
suggested_refs: Herwarth Walden's Der Sturm gallery, Kandinsky's pre-war Berlin dealer

stops.name: Weimar, taken onto the Bauhaus faculty
stops.date_confidence: Kandinsky begins teaching in June 1922; one consulted source dates Gropius's invitation to 1921. Day defaulted. The pin is inherited from itten.journey.json for coherence with the atlas; German Wikipedia puts the Van-de-Velde building at 50.97448, 11.32905, about 550 m south-east, and the discrepancy is left for the operator
stops.campa: Walter Gropius brings him to the Staatliches Bauhaus as a Formmeister. He is fifty-five. He is given the wall-painting workshop and teaches analytical drawing along with a course in the elements of colour and form, and he circulates a questionnaire through the school asking which colour belongs to the triangle, which to the square, which to the circle. Johannes Itten, whose preliminary course runs on breathing exercises and Mazdaznan diet, leaves within the year. The school is left with one colour system, and it is Kandinsky's.
stops.quote: A yellow triangle, a blue circle, a green square, or a green triangle, a yellow circle, a blue square--all these are different and have different spiritual values.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's Bauhaus colour questionnaire of 1923 and the wall-painting workshop
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Weimar, Die Blaue Vier assembled for America
stops.date_confidence: CORRECTED: German Wikipedia's 'Die Blaue Vier' dates the founding to March 1924 at Weimar, brought together and named by Galka Scheyer, against paul_klee.journey.json which gives 1923; the contradiction is flagged rather than resolved. Day defaulted
stops.campa: A dealer from Braunschweig, Galka Scheyer, gathers four painters into a group made for the American market and names it after the old one: Die Blaue Vier. Kandinsky, Klee, Lyonel Feininger, and Alexej von Jawlensky, who had drawn beside him in Azbe's school twenty-seven years earlier. Scheyer sails for New York and then California and spends the rest of her life selling the four of them to Americans who have never heard of any of them. The first United States show opens in New York in 1925.
suggested_refs: Galka Scheyer's Blue Four papers and the 1925 Charles Daniel Gallery exhibition, New York

stops.name: Dessau, the school moved and the course hardened
stops.date_confidence: the Thuringian government's pressure closes the Weimar school and the Bauhaus moves to Dessau in 1925; the month is approximate. The coordinate follows German Wikipedia for the Bauhausgebaeude, correcting a pin about 340 m too far east
stops.campa: Right-wing votes in Thuringia cut the school's money and the Bauhaus moves to Dessau, into a glass-walled building Gropius designs for it and finishes in 1926. He is fifty-eight. Kandinsky teaches the elementary course in form and colour, which every entering student is required to sit, and the system hardens as he teaches it: yellow to the triangle, red to the square, blue to the circle, then weight, tension, direction, the diagonal that resists and the one that falls.
stops.quote: Form, in the narrow sense, is nothing but the separating line between surfaces of colour.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: The Bauhaus Dessau building by Walter Gropius, and Kandinsky's elementary course in form and colour

stops.name: Dessau, the wall shared with Klee
stops.date_confidence: occupancy from 1926 is attested; the July date and the coordinate are both inherited byte-identical from paul_klee.journey.json, and the coordinate matches German Wikipedia's figure for the Meisterhaeuser on the Ebertallee
stops.campa: He and Nina take one half of a semi-detached Masters' House on the Ebertallee designed by Gropius, and the other half is Klee's. The two of them have known each other since Stuck's class in 1900. They paint their own walls in flat blocks of colour of their own choosing, share a garden fence for five years, and teach against each other's methods without falling out. Marcel Breuer builds a second tubular steel chair for Kandinsky's rooms because Kandinsky admires the first one.
stops.quote: a great artist and a lucid, pure human being
stops.quote_source: Kandinsky on Klee, in Bauhaus. Zeitschrift fuer Gestaltung, 1931, on Klee's departure for Duesseldorf; fragment as cited in paul_klee.journey.json
suggested_refs: The Meisterhaeuser on the Ebertallee, Dessau, and Breuer's Model B3 chair made in duplicate for Kandinsky's quarters

stops.name: Dessau, Point and Line to Plane
stops.date_confidence: published in 1926 as Bauhausbuch 9; the month is approximate and the day defaulted
stops.campa: Punkt und Linie zu Flaeche appears as the ninth Bauhaus book. It begins with the point, the smallest and most silent of marks, and builds through the line, which is a point that has been moved by a force, to the plane on which everything lands. The vocabulary of 1911 is still in it, but it now comes with diagrams and exercises, and the diagrams can be argued with. Fifteen years earlier he wrote that the spiritual triangle moves upward. Here he measures what a diagonal does to the corner it runs into.
stops.quote: A triangle (without the accessory consideration of its being acute-or obtuse-angled or equilateral) has a spiritual value of its own.
stops.quote_source: Wassily Kandinsky, Concerning the Spiritual in Art, trans. M. T. H. Sadler (1914)
suggested_refs: Punkt und Linie zu Flaeche, Bauhausbuch 9, Munich, 1926

stops.name: Friedrich-Theater, Pictures at an Exhibition staged
stops.date_confidence: the Dessau staging is dated to April 1928; the exact day is not established in any source reached and 4 April is supplied to order the segment. The theatre no longer stands and the pin is an approximate Dessau placeholder
stops.campa: He stages Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition at the Friedrich-Theater in Dessau in the spring of 1928 and designs all sixteen scenes himself. He is sixty-one. In most of them there are no dancers at all: only forms that move, colour thrown by lamps, black grounds, shapes hauled across the stage on wires. Der gelbe Klang has been waiting nineteen years for a stage and will not get one. This gets one. He sits in the house and watches his own painting move to music.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's staging of Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition, Friedrich-Theater Dessau, April 1928

stops.name: Berlin-Steglitz, the last Bauhaus in a telephone factory
stops.date_confidence: the Dessau council closes the school in 1932; Mies reopens it privately in a Berlin factory, police seal the building in April 1933, and the faculty vote to dissolve it that July. The 20 July date is the usually reported dissolution and was not independently confirmed; the Birkbuschstrasse address comes from general knowledge
stops.campa: The Nazi majority on the Dessau council shuts the school in 1932. Mies van der Rohe reopens it privately in a disused telephone factory in Berlin-Steglitz, and Kandinsky teaches there among the machine bays until the police seal the building in April and the faculty vote to dissolve the school themselves rather than run it on the conditions offered. He is sixty-six. Germany has been his working country for thirty-seven years and he has never held its passport.
suggested_refs: The final Bauhaus at Birkbuschstrasse, Berlin-Steglitz, and its self-dissolution in July 1933
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Neuilly-sur-Seine, a studio that is a living room
stops.date_confidence: the move to Neuilly at the end of 1933 is attested and the place of death matches; the coordinate estimates the boulevard de la Seine and the building was not identified this pass. Day defaulted
stops.campa: They take a small flat at Neuilly-sur-Seine on the boulevard de la Seine, and he works in the living room because there is no studio. He is sixty-seven and beginning a third country. The canvases made in these rooms let go of the Bauhaus right angle: soft grounds of pink and turquoise, and floating on them small signs like embryos, larvae, things seen down a lens. The geometry has gone biological and nobody in Paris quite knows where to file him. He takes scientific journals and cuts out the plates of protozoa.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's late Paris canvases, 1934-1944, and the biological plates he collected

stops.name: Paris, the nephew writes on the uncle
stops.date_confidence: [R] Alexandre Kojeve, born Aleksandr Kozhevnikov, is described in the dossier and in standard Kojeve biography as Kandinsky's nephew and published an essay on his painting; neither the family tie nor the essay's date was re-verified from a primary source in this pass. Year approximate, day defaulted. The pin is the atlas's canonical Paris coordinate
stops.campa: His nephew Aleksandr Kozhevnikov, who in Paris calls himself Alexandre Kojeve, writes an essay on the uncle's painting. Its argument is that these canvases are not abstract at all but concrete: they abstract from no object, being themselves the object, and there is nothing behind them to be faithful to. In the same years Kojeve is running the Hegel seminar that much of French philosophy attends. Kandinsky is twenty minutes west at Neuilly, painting the very pictures the essay describes.
suggested_refs: Alexandre Kojeve, 'Les peintures concretes de Kandinsky', and the Kojeve material later acquired by the Kandinsky Society
sources: dossier synthesis, family tie flagged for primary confirmation

stops.name: Neuilly, the news from Munich
stops.date_confidence: the Entartete Kunst exhibition opens in Munich 19 July 1937 and closes 30 November; German Wikipedia gives 57 Kandinsky works confiscated from German museums and 14 of them shown in Munich. He is at Neuilly and did not travel to it: the stop sits at his own pin and takes the exhibition's opening date
stops.campa: In Munich, the city where he learned to draw, an exhibition called Entartete Kunst opens with the pictures hung crooked and the sums the public museums paid for them painted on the wall alongside. Fifty-seven of his own works have been taken out of German collections and fourteen of them are in those rooms. He is at Neuilly and does not see it. Two million people do. The German market that had bought him since Der Sturm closes inside one summer, and what is not destroyed is sold abroad for foreign currency.
suggested_refs: The Entartete Kunst exhibition, Munich, 19 July to 30 November 1937, and the confiscation inventories of German public collections
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Galerie Renou et Colle, looking at Frida Kahlo's pictures
stops.date_confidence: attested to 10 March 1939. The pin is the atlas's canonical Paris coordinate, inherited byte-identical from frida_kahlo.journey.json and diego_rivera.journey.json; the gallery's own address is not separately pinned
stops.campa: Marcel Duchamp hangs a Mexican show at the Galerie Renou et Colle, with seventeen paintings by Frida Kahlo in it among the pre-Columbian objects and the retablos. Kandinsky comes to look, and so does Picasso. He is seventy-two, thirty-nine years past Stuck's drawing class, standing in front of the work of a painter born the year he finished Concerning the Spiritual in Art. It is March 1939. Within eighteen months the gallery is shut and Paris belongs to the German army.
suggested_refs: The Mexique exhibition, Galerie Renou et Colle, Paris, March 1939

stops.name: Neuilly, death in the flat on the boulevard
stops.date_confidence: attested to 13 December 1944 at Neuilly-sur-Seine. The naturalisation of 1939 is attested; one consulted source claims he gained German citizenship in 1928, which contradicts the standard account that he never naturalised German, and that contradiction is recorded rather than resolved
stops.campa: He took French citizenship in 1939 and sat out the occupation in the flat at Neuilly, painting on cardboard and on small boards because canvas could not be had, and refusing the offers to leave for America. He is seventy-seven, and Nina is forty-five. His last exhibition during his life opens at the Galerie L'Esquisse in occupied Paris. He dies at home on 13 December 1944, six months after the city was liberated and five before the war in Europe ends.
suggested_refs: Kandinsky's last lifetime exhibition, Galerie L'Esquisse, Paris, 1944
sources: The Art Story, 'Kandinsky: Life and Legacy'

stops.name: Nanterre, Division 16 rang 35
stops.date_confidence: the grave is Division 16, rang 35 of the Cimetiere nouveau de Neuilly-sur-Seine per French Wikipedia. CORRECTED: that cemetery is not in Neuilly but over the boundary at 40 rue de Vimy, Nanterre, with grounds running into Puteaux, and the coordinate is corrected about 1.5 km north-west from a pin that fell inside Neuilly proper. The day of burial is not attested and is supplied to order the segment
stops.campa: He is buried in the new cemetery of Neuilly-sur-Seine, which is not in Neuilly: it lies over the commune boundary in Nanterre with its gate on the rue de Vimy, and its grounds run on into Puteaux. Division sixteen, row thirty-five. He is buried in a suburb he came to at sixty-seven because Germany had stopped being possible, in a country whose citizenship he took at seventy-two, five years before the burial and forty-three after he first left Russia. Nina, killed in her Swiss chalet thirty-six years later, goes into the same grave.
suggested_refs: The Kandinsky grave, Division 16 rang 35, Cimetiere nouveau de Neuilly-sur-Seine at Nanterre

stops.name: Lenbachhaus, what Gabriele Muenter kept
stops.date_confidence: attested to 19 February 1957, Muenter's eightieth birthday. CORRECTED: the gift is more than 90 Kandinsky oils, not the more than 80 given in an earlier pass, and the coordinate is Luisenstrasse 33 per German Wikipedia, not the pin used earlier
stops.campa: On her eightieth birthday Gabriele Muenter hands the city of Munich what she has held since 1914: more than ninety Kandinsky oils, over three hundred and thirty watercolours and drawings, the sketchbooks, the reverse-glass paintings, nearly all the prints, together with twenty-five of her own canvases and works by Jawlensky, Marc, Macke and Werefkin. A settlement in 1926 had left her the legal owner. It sat in the cellar at Murnau through the Nazi years while she told the authorities she had sold everything long ago.
suggested_refs: The Gabriele Muenter and Johannes Eichner Foundation, Staedtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus, Munich
sources: Lenbachhaus, 'Gabriele Muenter and Johannes Eichner Foundation'

stops.name: Guggenheim Museum, The Yellow Sound performed at last
stops.date_confidence: attested to 12 May 1972 as the generally accepted world premiere. The pin is inherited byte-identical from frank_lloyd_wright.journey.json, hilma_af_klint.journey.json and cecilia_vicuna.journey.json
stops.campa: Der gelbe Klang is performed. It was written around 1909; the Munich production collapsed when war broke out in 1914, a Bauhaus attempt came to nothing, a third German plan failed. Sixty-three years after it was written and twenty-eight after his death, the giants and the coloured light and the wordless voices are put on a stage in New York, inside the museum built to hold the non-objective painting that Hilla Rebay and Solomon Guggenheim had been buying from him since 1929.
suggested_refs: The 12 May 1972 premiere of Der gelbe Klang, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York

stops.name: Centre Pompidou, the widow's bequest
stops.date_confidence: Nina Kandinsky is murdered at her chalet at Gstaad on 2 September 1980, robbery suspected, nobody convicted; her handwritten will of January 1980 leaves the studio holdings to the Musee national d'art moderne and the bequest takes effect in 1981. One museum source dates her death to 1981, which is the year of the bequest and not of the death, so the apparent contradiction is a conflation. Day defaulted
stops.campa: Nina Kandinsky is killed at her chalet at Gstaad in September 1980, jewellery taken, the case never closed. Her will of that January leaves everything still in her hands to the Musee national d'art moderne: paintings, watercolours, drawings, prints, papers, the contents of the studio. It reaches the Centre Pompidou the following year and makes the most complete Kandinsky holding anywhere. The society she set up to manage the work goes on buying related material, some of it from Kojeve's estate, until it is wound up in 2015.
suggested_refs: The Nina Kandinsky bequest to the Musee national d'art moderne, and the Societe Kandinsky, 1979-2015
sources: Google Arts and Culture / Centre Pompidou, 'What Happened to Kandinsky's Belongings'

stops.name: Amsterdam, Bild mit Haeusern given back
stops.date_confidence: CORRECTED: the Frederik Muller sale is 9 October 1940, not the 8-9 October of an earlier pass; the hammer price is 160 guilders, 176 with the buyer's premium. The Restitutions Committee rejects the heirs' claim on 22 October 2018 and the city hands the painting over on 27 February 2022. The 2023 sale price of Murnau mit Kirche II is carried from press reporting and was not verified against an auction house
stops.campa: Bild mit Haeusern, painted at Murnau in 1909, was sold in occupied Amsterdam in October 1940 out of the dispossessed Lewenstein family and bought by the city museum for a hundred and seventy-six guilders. The heirs asked for it back. In 2018 the Dutch Restitutions Committee weighed the museum's interest against theirs and let the city keep it; the assessment framework was rewritten after the argument that followed, and in February 2022 the picture went to the heirs. Murnau mit Kirche II, restituted by the Van Abbemuseum, sold in 2023 for a reported 37.2 million pounds.
suggested_refs: Restitutiecommissie binding opinion on Bild mit Haeusern; Stedelijk Museum news release, 27 February 2022
sources: Restitutiecommissie.nl, recommendation on Bild mit Haeusern
Stedelijk Museum, 'Painting Kandinsky handed over to heirs'
